revenue_segments.name: Digital
revenue_segments.commentary: Growth came from higher sales of exploration data licenses and transfer fees (Digital Exploration +25%, or $25M, QoQ) and Platforms & Applications (+$17M QoQ). Pretax margin was 28%, up 683 bps QoQ.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q Q2 2026, Note 12 Segment Information; Item 2 MD&A, Digital

revenue_segments.name: Reservoir Performance
revenue_segments.commentary: Lower evaluation, stimulation and intervention activity from Middle East conflict disruptions. Some countries began to recover, but production shut-ins and security challenges constrained others. Pretax margin was 15%, down 121 bps QoQ.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q Q2 2026, Note 12 Segment Information; Item 2 MD&A, Reservoir Performance

revenue_segments.name: Well Construction
revenue_segments.commentary: Middle East disruptions were partly offset by higher offshore drilling in Latin America. Pretax margin was 15%, flat QoQ. For six months, the margin was down 401 bps YoY on lower Middle East profitability and pricing headwinds in select markets.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q Q2 2026, Note 12 Segment Information; Item 2 MD&A, Well Construction

revenue_segments.name: Production Systems
revenue_segments.commentary: The YoY increase reflects the acquired ChampionX production chemicals and artificial lift businesses. Sequential growth came from SLB OneSubsea, artificial lift, valves, surface production systems and completions. Pretax margin was 16%, up 138 bps QoQ. Excluding ChampionX, six-month revenue fell 3% YoY.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q Q2 2026, Note 12 Segment Information; Item 2 MD&A, Production Systems

revenue_segments.name: All Other
revenue_segments.commentary: The sequential gain was driven by Data Center Solutions revenue (+33%, or $46M). The YoY six-month decline reflects the absence of $215M of APS revenue after the Palliser divestiture and lower SLB Capturi revenue.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q Q2 2026, Note 12 Segment Information; Item 2 MD&A, All Other

forward_guidance.text: The only quantitative outlook in the 10-Q is that full-year 2026 capital investments (capex, APS investments and capitalized exploration data) are expected to be approximately $2.5 billion. SLB believes cash and short-term investments of $4.1 billion plus $5.0 billion of undrawn committed credit facilities are sufficient for the next 12 months and beyond. No revenue, margin or EPS guidance is given in this filing.

key_risks.description: ChampionX integration execution and realization of synergies. Merger & integration charges were $69M in Q2 and $110M for six months, and amortization expense rose to $111M in Q2 from $82M.

bull_case: Revenue rose 3% QoQ to $8.97B despite a 13% QoQ drop in Middle East revenue. Excluding the Middle East, revenue grew sequentially across all Divisions, led by offshore activity in Latin America, Europe & Africa and Asia.

Production Systems is the growth engine: revenue was +29% YoY (including ChampionX), pretax margin expanded 138 bps QoQ to 16%, and ChampionX contributed $1.7B revenue and $307M pretax income in the first half.
Digital pretax income rose to $194M (28% margin) from $134M in Q1, and Data Center Solutions revenue grew 33% QoQ, a new growth vector.
Backlog was $6.4B, with about 70% expected to convert to revenue within 12 months, and Middle East activity began recovering in certain countries.
Strong shareholder returns and liquidity: dividend raised 3.5%, $648M repurchased in Q2 at about $54 per share, $4.1B of cash and investments, and $5.0B of undrawn credit facilities.
Interest & other income improved sequentially to $76M from $43M, and Q2 pretax income rose to $1,019M from $956M in Q1.
bear_case: Q2 diluted EPS of $0.52 was down 30% from $0.74 a year ago. Net income fell 22% while the diluted share count rose about 10% on the ChampionX all-stock deal.
Excluding ChampionX, six-month revenue fell 6% (about $1.05B) YoY, and Reservoir Performance (-8%) and Well Construction (-7%) both declined YoY in Q2 with lower margins.
Middle East disruption is ongoing, with revenue down 13% QoQ and about 12% YoY for six months. Timing of recovery is uncertain given continued production shut-ins and security challenges.

Free cash flow of $693M for six months was below the prior year, while buybacks plus dividends were about $2.0B. Net debt rose $1.3B to $8.7B, and net debt was funded partly by $2.0B of new long-term debt.
Margin compression: six-month pretax margins fell for Well Construction (-401 bps), Reservoir Performance (-208 bps) and Production Systems (-178 bps), with pricing headwinds in select markets.

Higher D&A (six months $1,397M vs $1,273M) and amortization of acquired intangibles (about $449M annually in 2027) weigh on earnings. Q2 2025 also included a $149M APS gain, so YoY comparisons of other income are difficult.

what_to_watch.text: Pace of Middle East recovery: whether sequential revenue stabilizes from $1.66B and which countries remain constrained by shut-ins and security issues. Also the effect on Reservoir Performance and Well Construction margins.
Production Systems momentum: SLB OneSubsea, artificial lift and valves growth, plus ChampionX integration costs and synergies (merger & integration charges were $69M in Q2).
Offshore activity in Latin America, Europe & Africa and Asia, and the conversion of the $6.4B backlog.
Digital Exploration data license sales (lumpy) and Data Center Solutions growth, and whether Digital's 28% margin is sustainable.
Free cash flow generation and working capital (receivables, inventories) against $2.5B full-year capex, net debt of $8.7B, and the buyback pace (about $3.0B remaining authorization).
Pricing trends and margin recovery in Well Construction and Reservoir Performance, and any management commentary on 2026 guidance on the next earnings call.
